reason: Both probes stay incomplete (bgImage), so I measured the worst case by hand. On cards.issue-card the flagged Jane Black label is white (#fff) on the dark card art; with the text hidden, the lightest background pixel under it is rgb(43,43,62), which gives 13.8:1 against the 4.5:1 needed. On billpay.inbox-zero the flagged element is the native file input of the Bill Pay drop zone at opacity 0.00001: its Choose Files text is not visible, so there is no visible text to fail.

Reproduced: Tab reaches the Agent Card checkbox input, which is opacity 0 (probe-8bc95bbd3dc5: visible false, hidden invisible). But the input sits inside a label whose :focus-within style draws a 3px ring, rgb(112,115,147) against white at 4.6:1, around the whole Agent Card row. Focusing the checkbox changed 1,924 pixels, all around that row, so a keyboard user sees where focus is.
criterionAnalysis: 2.4.7 Focus Visible: the checkbox is a visually hidden native input that has a custom box beside it, and the label draws a visible ring on the whole row when the input has focus, so a keyboard focus indicator is visible and the criterion is met. The sweep measured the input itself, which is invisible by design, not the control's indicator. 2.4.3 Focus Order: stop 9 of 15 follows the Virtual or Physical radios and precedes the Control type combobox, in visual order, so the order is meaningful. 1.4.11 does not fail: the ring is 4.6:1 against its neighbor.

reason: The Control type combobox carries autocomplete="garbage" next to data-1p-ignore, data-lpignore and data-bwignore, a deliberate switch-off of browser autofill. Control type is a spend-control category picker, not a field about the user, so no 1.3.5 input purpose applies on either sampled state.
criterionAnalysis: 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose applies only to fields that collect information about the user and whose purpose is one of the 53 listed input purposes. Control type picks a spend-control category for a card, which no listed purpose covers, so the invalid token does not make 1.3.5 fail. The token is ignored by browsers and the accessibility tree exposes combobox 'Control type' with its name and state intact, so 4.1.2 is not affected either.

reason: The Cardholder combobox carries autocomplete="garbage" next to data-1p-ignore, data-lpignore and data-bwignore, a deliberate switch-off of browser autofill. It picks which team member receives the card (placeholder Select a team member), so it does not collect the signed-in user's own name and no 1.3.5 input purpose applies on either sampled state.
criterionAnalysis: 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose applies to fields that collect information about the user and map to one of the listed purposes. Cardholder is a picker of team members, and an admin can choose someone else, so a name or cc-name token would be wrong for it. The invalid token is ignored by browsers, and the accessibility tree exposes combobox 'Cardholder' with its name and state, so 4.1.2 is not affected either.

reason: Reproduced: the Control type combobox has aria-invalid=true and aria-errormessage pointing at a plain span (Please complete this field) with no role, no aria-live and no aria-describedby; Chrome's tree does resolve it (errormessage=Please complete this field). Screen readers that do not support aria-errormessage will not read the text when the field gets focus, and the error is also visible beside the field, so impact is minor. The missed announcement on submit is the separate status-message finding.
